**Instructions.** Choose the single best answer (a–e) for each question. You may use a periodic table.
Calculators are allowed. Answers are rounded to the precision shown. Time yourself: aim for about 30 minutes
(roughly 2 minutes per question, the same pace as the full exam).

**Answer sheet.** Use the bubble answer sheet (`CHEM1301/exam-prep/answer-sheet/answer-sheet.pdf`), rows 1–15.

```{=latex}
\needspace{9\baselineskip}
```
**1.** While finding an empirical formula, you divide by the smallest mole value and get C 1.00, H 1.33, O 1.00. What should you do next?

```{=latex}
\begingroup\leftskip=1.5em
```
a)\ Divide every result by 1.33 again\
b)\ Multiply every element's result by 3, giving C~3~H~4~O~3~\
c)\ Multiply every result by 2, giving C~2~H~3~O~2~\
d)\ Multiply only the H result by 3, giving CH~4~O\
e)\ Round H to 1, giving CHO

```{=latex}
\par\endgroup\medskip
```

```{=latex}
\needspace{9\baselineskip}
```
**2.** Erythrose has the molecular formula C~4~H~8~O~4~. What is its empirical formula?

```{=latex}
\begingroup\leftskip=1.5em
```
a)\ CH~4~O\
b)\ C~4~H~8~O~4~\
c)\ CHO\
d)\ CH~2~O\
e)\ C~2~H~4~O~2~

```{=latex}
\par\endgroup\medskip
```

```{=latex}
\needspace{9\baselineskip}
```
**3.** Aspirin is 60.00% C, 4.48% H, and 35.52% O by mass. What is its empirical formula?

```{=latex}
\begingroup\leftskip=1.5em
```
a)\ C~2~H~2~O\
b)\ C~18~H~16~O~8~\
c)\ C~9~H~2~O\
d)\ C~13~HO~8~\
e)\ C~9~H~8~O~4~

```{=latex}
\par\endgroup\medskip
```

```{=latex}
\needspace{9\baselineskip}
```

**7.** A liquid fuel is 52.14% C, 13.13% H, and 34.73% O by mass, and its molar mass is 46.07 g/mol. It burns completely in O~2~ to form CO~2~ and H~2~O. How many moles of O~2~ are needed to burn 0.200 mol of the fuel?

```{=latex}
\begingroup\leftskip=1.5em
```
a)\ 0.200 mol\
b)\ 0.400 mol\
c)\ 0.600 mol\
d)\ 0.700 mol\
e)\ 1.20 mol

```{=latex}
\par\endgroup\medskip
```

```{=latex}
\needspace{9\baselineskip}
```
**8.** To convert **moles of A** into **moles of B** for a reaction, which information do you need?

```{=latex}
\begingroup\leftskip=1.5em
```
a)\ The coefficients of A and B in the balanced equation\
b)\ Avogadro's number\
c)\ The masses of A and B present\
d)\ The molar masses of A and B\
e)\ The subscripts in the formulas of A and B

```{=latex}
\par\endgroup\medskip
```

```{=latex}
\needspace{9\baselineskip}
```

```{=latex}
\begingroup\leftskip=1.5em
```
a)\ 1.20 mol\

c)\ 2.40 mol\

```{=latex}
\begingroup\leftskip=1.5em
```
a)\ 0.157 g\
b)\ 4.24 g\
c)\ 8.49 g\
d)\ 10.0 g\
e)\ 17.0 g

```{=latex}
\par\endgroup\medskip
```

**12.** Potassium burns according to the **unbalanced** equation K(s) + O~2~(g) $\rightarrow$ K~2~O(s). What mass of K~2~O forms from 7.82 g of K with excess O~2~?

```{=latex}
\begingroup\leftskip=1.5em
```
a)\ 0.100 g\
b)\ 3.91 g\
c)\ 4.71 g\
d)\ 9.42 g\
e)\ 18.8 g

```{=latex}
\par\endgroup\medskip
```

**13.** Zinc sulfide is roasted: 2ZnS(s) + 3O~2~(g) $\rightarrow$ 2ZnO(s) + 2SO~2~(g). A mixture of 50.0 g of ZnS and 20.0 g of O~2~ reacts. Which statement is correct?

```{=latex}
\begingroup\leftskip=1.5em
```
a)\ ZnS is limiting, and O~2~ is left over\
b)\ O~2~ is limiting, and 9.40 g of ZnS is left over\
c)\ O~2~ is limiting, and 50.0 g of ZnS is left over\
d)\ O~2~ is limiting, and 40.6 g of ZnS is left over\
e)\ Neither is limiting; both reactants are used up completely

```{=latex}
\par\endgroup\medskip
```

```{=latex}
\needspace{9\baselineskip}
```
**14.** For 2Al(s) + 3CuSO~4~(aq) $\rightarrow$ Al~2~(SO~4~)~3~(aq) + 3Cu(s), 5.40 g of Al reacts with 40.0 g of CuSO~4~. What is the theoretical yield of Cu?

```{=latex}
\begingroup\leftskip=1.5em
```
a)\ 0.251 g\
b)\ 15.9 g\
c)\ 19.1 g\
d)\ 40.0 g\
e)\ 45.4 g

```{=latex}
\par\endgroup\medskip
```

```{=latex}
\needspace{9\baselineskip}
```

```{=latex}
\begingroup\leftskip=1.5em
```
a)\ 0.881%\
b)\ 17.6%\
c)\ 88.1%\

e)\ 146%
